prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System(CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hours; protection overrides regulation; automatic movement requires trusted communications. Operations Control Centre’s Line Traffic Controller owns recovery/incidents/regulation; restricts untrusted control; cybersecurity restrictions/mode-changes require notification. Recovery: confirmed positions; automatic return: trusted communications, verified routes/positions, recorded handback. Signal Maintenance Engineer(Maple)/controller concur on occupancy/route resets; engineer verifies manual-route protection; security-sensitive access requires Cyber Security Officer approval. East Junction Interlocking(Falcon) supplies Axle Counter Reset Request, proves/holds routes/points until safe-release confirmation; no locked/approach reset; rejects invalid-signature/expired-certificate/out-of-window messages. West Junction Interlocking supplies Route Release Exception List; rejects protection conflicts. North District Zone Controller(Marble)/South District Zone Controller(Orchid) validate separation/authority/locking; transfers require odometry/validation/reissue; North validates Temporary Speed Restriction Notice limits; South inhibits automatic routing with manually-confirmed occupancy. Atlas Onboard Controller(Kestrel): initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train-operation/fallback/cutout; enforces authority/speed/doors/braking; reports faults/checksums/readiness. Dual Channel Odometer disagreement invalidates location; uncertain location/missing authority requires restricted-manual. Train Radio Modem reports loss; Wayside Radio Access Network failure requires throughput reduction. Voice Dispatch Console authorizes restrictions; Revenue Train Operator repeats instructions, sends Test Train Clearance Memo; cab security-awareness, no passenger-service cybersecurity administration. Platform Screen Door Controller: protected-local until stopping verified. Metro Operations Control System(Lantern) sends Crew Login Token Bundle; distinguishes command/lock/occupancy; preserves alarms; memo prerequisite for protected non-revenue security exceptions. Service Timetable Server supplies context; Passenger Information Gateway receives reconciled predictions/platform-updates. Maintenance Diagnostic Server(Quarry) retains/protects evidence, compares Brake Curve Checksum Log; cannot bypass trust. Cyber Security Officer continuously correlates Safety Data Communication Network/radio/Lantern events without altering safety paths; classifies availability alerts by impact/territory/authority; investigates audit file. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance controls certificates: approved identity/baseline/domain/service; pre-expiry renewal; compromise/retirement/unreconciled-maintenance revocation; named-account/MFA/separated-duty/approved administration. Audit evidence: synchronized

New part:
S218: Audit records shall be protected from local alteration by the component that generates them and shall be retained for the period defined by Greenvale Metro governance.
S219: The Service Timetable Server and Passenger Information Gateway shall be monitored for compromise because incorrect operational context can influence control room decisions even when safety commands remain valid.
S220: The Voice Dispatch Console shall be included in security incident procedures when a cyber event changes the normal method for issuing operational instructions.
S221: The Platform Screen Door Controller shall accept only authenticated interfaces approved for passenger service coordination and maintenance testing.
S222: The Dual Channel Odometer and Atlas Onboard Controller shall report security-relevant diagnostic conditions in a manner that supports investigation without exposing cryptographic material.
S223: Security responsibilities shall be reviewed after major timetable changes, radio coverage modifications, control center upgrades, or any incident that questions the integrity of safety-related communications.
S224: Commissioning shall begin only after the installed equipment baseline for the Atlas Onboard Controller, Dual Channel Odometer, Train Radio Modem, and wayside control equipment has been configuration checked against the approved release record.
S225: The test-train phase shall use non-passenger movements to prove train localization, movement authority processing, braking response, radio continuity, and operator displays under controlled operating conditions.
S226: Each test train shall be crewed by a Revenue Train Operator qualified for commissioning duties and supported by a Line Traffic Controller with authority to stop the trial when observed conditions depart from the approved script.
S227: Initial movements shall be conducted at restricted commissioning speeds and shall progress to representative service speeds only after the Atlas Onboard Controller and North District Zone Controller demonstrate stable supervision.
S228: The South District Zone Controller shall be commissioned under the same test regime so that boundary behavior is verified before whole-line operation is attempted.
S229: East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking shall remain under enhanced monitoring during migration because route setting, point detection, and authority release behavior are critical to mixed-mode operation.
S230: The staged migration from legacy signalling shall divide the railway into controlled areas that can be commissioned, operated, and, if necessary, returned to legacy control without affecting uncommissioned areas.
S231: Cutover planning shall define the exact control boundaries, permissible train movements, staffing levels, and rollback conditions for each migration stage.
S232: Before any cutover stage, the Safety Data Communication Network and Wayside Radio Access Network shall be verified for coverage, latency, redundancy, and alarm presentation at the control center.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
